From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Cutover governance & docs triage — final alignment before prod ramp

Team —

We have one remaining internal sweep before the prod ramp for the Acme Retail integration. I attached cutover_playbook_v3.docx and the current cutover matrix (link below). I need confirmation on the following by EOD Wed 10/21 so we can lock the playbook and start enablement scheduling: 

1) Doc ownership: who owns final runbook & rollback steps (master file in Drive).
2) Exception approval path: for SLA exceptions, billing credits, or scope pushes — who signs off and what are the thresholds (financial/SLO).
3) Cutover triggers / rollback gates: precise telemetry thresholds (error rate, 95th latency) that auto-trigger rollback.
4) Training & enablement: final trainer, recorded slot, and runbook walkthrough date.
5) Ops on-call coverage during cutover window and handover notes.

Quick context: Acme’s launch window is currently planned for 2026-11-03 02:00–06:00 PT (low-traffic window). We need final doc/owner signoffs + exception routing in place before we schedule the production DR drill.

Relevant links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A1CutoverPlaybook (master playbook)
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1283

Attachments: cutover_playbook_v3.docx (master playbook, includes checklist & telemetry thresholds)

Thanks — please call out any unresolved blockers in your replies.

—Naomi

Subject: Re: Cutover governance & docs triage — final alignment before prod ramp

Naomi — thanks for the clear list. A few quick notes from infra/ops: 

- Runbook owner: I can own the pre-cutover runbook and post-cutover validation sections, but we should assign a single owner for the entire document (including coordinator duties) — recommend Marissa or Vanessa as primary doc steward.
- QA signoff: must be explicit in the playbook. Add a "QA green" checklist item (smoke tests + synthetic traffic ramp) that is required before the cutover start.
- Rollback gates: propose the following quick thresholds for discussion: error rate > 2.5% sustained over 3 minutes OR 95th latency > 1.5s sustained over 5 minutes triggers immediate rollback. We'll surface these in the telemetry runbook.
- Ops coverage: I'll schedule the on-call rotation for the window; need the final list of participants to post on-call Slack channel.

Happy to take runbook ownership for infra sections. Assign the document to me and I’ll push edits to the Drive file.

Ben

Forwarded attachment: sla-exception-template.pdf (see stub)

Fwd: quick routing process proposal below — keeping it tight since execs will want a single path for approvals.

Proposed exception routing (TL;DR):
- Routine exceptions (non-financial, ops impact only): Product Manager + Platform Ops (Marissa + Naomi) can approve up to $5k-equivalent remediation or minor SLA credits.
- Medium exceptions (financial impact between $5k–$50k or partial SLA credits): requires Platform Ops + Finance (cc: finance lead) signoff. Escalate to Karthik for technical risk assessment.
- Major exceptions (> $50k or systemic SLA risk): requires VP Product + VP Ops (Naomi & Karthik) and Legal review.

I attached the sla-exception-template.pdf for the routing form we should use. It contains required fields: impact estimate, affected customers, rollback plan, and mandatory QA evidence.

Also: customer-facing FAQ draft attached to Drive (I'll put it in the FAQ folder by EOD 10/22).

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

- Rollback gates: accept Ben’s thresholds for the runbook (error >2.5% over 3m, 95th >1.5s over 5m).

- Cutover window: confirmed for 2026-11-03 02:00–06:00 PT.
